title: Lesion atlas: right heart (pulmonary stenosis and atresia, Ebstein anomaly, tricuspid dysplasia)

items.question: The four-chamber view looks normal, but the three-vessel view shows reversed flow in the ductus. Which right-sided obstructive lesion is among the possibilities?
items.explanation: In pulmonary stenosis the four-chamber view may look normal while reversed colour flow is seen in the ductus or main PA. This sign is not diagnostic on its own: it is a reason to complete the study, not a final diagnosis.

items.question: What does reversed ductal flow suggest in pulmonary stenosis?
options: Mild disease that needs no follow-up
items.explanation: Reversed ductal flow suggests ductal dependence.

items.question: Pulmonary atresia with a small right ventricle. How do you look for coronary fistulae?
options: Low-velocity colour Doppler for to-and-fro flow in the right ventricular free wall or septum
High-velocity colour scale on the aortic arch
They cannot be seen before birth
items.explanation: Fistulae are suspected when low-velocity colour shows to-and-fro flow in the RV free wall or septum.

items.question: Pulmonary stenosis with more than mild tricuspid regurgitation on colour. What does this suggest about sinusoids?
items.explanation: Tricuspid regurgitation greater than mild is associated with a low risk of sinusoids.

items.question: What is the first clue to Ebstein anomaly or tricuspid dysplasia?
items.explanation: Significant right atrial dilatation, with or without RV dilatation, is the first clue.

items.question: Severe tricuspid regurgitation; the pulmonary valve does not seem to open. Why is Doppler of the regurgitant jet critical?
options: To exclude primary pulmonary obstruction and gauge right ventricular pressure
To confirm that the valve is normal
items.explanation: PW and CW Doppler of the TR jet exclude primary pulmonary obstruction and show whether the RV can generate pressure; the RV may fail to open the valve (functional atresia).

items.question: Severe tricuspid disease with pulmonary atresia, structural or functional. Which ductal finding is always present?
items.explanation: It is always associated with retrograde ductal flow, which can develop at any point and must be documented serially.

items.question: Ebstein anomaly. Why measure the branch pulmonary arteries?
options: Their hypoplasia correlates with lung hypoplasia
items.explanation: Branch PA hypoplasia correlates with lung hypoplasia.

items.question: Ebstein anomaly. Which rhythm problems are common?
options: Complete heart block in every case
items.explanation: Atrial ectopy and supraventricular tachyarrhythmias are common, so rhythm should be assessed.

items.question: Pulmonary regurgitation with a patent ductus. What can result?
options: A circular shunt and placental steal
items.explanation: This combination can cause a circular shunt and placental steal.
